Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. Pakistan is seen in a huddle, near the ropes. Tom Latham and Chad Bowes are the openers for New Zealand. Shaheen Afridi to start with the ball. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, Pakistan have posted a good total of 193 runs on the board. They will be hoping for their bowlers to defend this one. For New Zealand, the onus is on their batters to put up a good stand and chase this down. Which side will get over the line? Let's find out together. Chase coming up shortly...

Blair Tickner is in for a quick chat. He says that he just tried a few variations early on and luckily it worked out. Mentions he was lucky enough to get the best of Azam. Adds that he was just trying to hit the hard length and is glad that it worked in his favor.

New Zealand will be upset with how things ended up for them. They just failed to get the wicket of Mohammad Rizwan who went on to score 98 runs for his side. Blair Tickner was the pick of the bowlers for them as he picked up three wickets. Ish Sodhi chipped in with one wicket. The rest of the bowlers were wicketless.

What a scintillating knock this has been from Mohammad Rizwan. He just fell shy of two runs in completing his century. He scored a knock of unbeaten 98 runs and made his side reach a good total of 193 runs. After being sent to bat first, the hosts started off well but lost their skipper just before the powerplay. Mohammad Haris and Saim Ayub soon followed the suit and the flurry of runs slowed down for a bit but Iftikhar Ahmed joined hands with Rizwan and played a good knock. After Iftikhar's dismissal, Imad Wasim played a good cameo alongside Rizwan and added crucial runs to the board.

BYE! Mohammad Rizwan walks off the field on 98, just a couple short of his ton, but he did the job for his side here. It is a slower bumper, on off. Mohammad Rizwan tries to heave it across the line but misses. They only collect a bye. Pakistan end their innings at 193/5.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! It is time for the series decider of the five-match T20I series between Pakistan and New Zealand. The hosts are leading the series, winning two games, whilst the visitors have won one.  The last match was a washout, as the series stands with the hosts leading it by 2-1.
... MATCH DAY ...

It has all come down to the 5th and final T20I of the 5-match T20 series between Pakistan and New Zealand. Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium will host this thriller between these two cricketing giants. Pakistan are coming into this game feeling a bit more at ease than their opponents, leading the series 2-1 with the washout in the previous game. The bowlers of Pakistan have been firing on all cylinders with the batters performing with the blade in their hands as well. The team has looked comfortable against the Kiwis and they would be stepping up into this game expecting to clinch the series. The hosts rely heavily on their top order to give them a solid start and would be relying on the services of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan yet again. The bowlers have always delivered for them and they would be hoping to continue the good form with the ball in their hands. The only headache for the hosts would be the batting order as Iftikhar Ahmed coming deep down at 8 in the 3rd T20I was an absolute shocker. New Zealand on the other hand, would be high on confidence as well with the top order finally clicking for them. Chad Bowes was outstanding in the previous game with the bat and the visitors would be hoping for something similar from the opener in this game as well. The bowling unit for the visitors has been a bit dull till now and the likes of Matt Henry and Adam Milne would be looking to bowl magical spells in the final T20I of this series to level it up. The game promises to be a thriller.
